correctness.rationale: For connected allocations, 2n(tr((L+P)^(-1))-1) is strictly convex and identifies unique edge weights by offdiagonal entries. Matching-preserving group symmetry reduces every global optimum to exactly two edge weights, with a positive nonmatching class. The complete Fourier/two-block spectrum leads to a scalar ratio objective. Its exact derivative is (n-1)D_n(r)(t-T_n(r)); since N_n'(r)D_n(r)-N_n(r)D_n'(r)=N_n'(r)/n-n²/(X³Y³)<0, it has the claimed unique minimizing ratio and threshold. The matrix-tree determinant comparison, strict positive threshold gap, and n→∞ limit are algebraic. A real script extracted from the new package reproduces 2094 finite checks; finite checks are supplementary, not proof.

The result provides globally unique allocations and full value for every n≥3, a price-threshold gap of order 1/n, and a positive limiting fraction of expenditure on discounted matching connections.
